text.p: Austrian high-grade steel maker Boehler-Uddeholm said on Tuesday 1996 group net profit fell 10 percent as its tax position worsened and sounded a cautious note for the current year.

The group said net earnings fell to 1.0 billion schilligs from 1.11 billion a year earlier as its tax rate rose to 25 percent from 18 percent last year. Pre-tax profits were steady at 1.35 billion schillings.
New orders fell 21 percent to 8.952 billion schillings, while order backlog fell 34 percent to 2.727 billion, Boehler said in a statement released ahead of a news conference.

The group said 1996 had nevertheless been "satisfactory, particularly considering that the overall conditions for the steel industry were significantly more unfavourable than in 1995 and that the market slump in Germany was much stronger than expected".

Boehler said that because of the "stable earnings and the confidence in the future development of the company" it would raise its 1996 dividend to 26 schillings per share, from 25 schillings a year earlier.
The group, which was privatised by the Austrian government in March of 1995, said it was cautious on the business outlook for the current year as overall market conditions remained sluggish.
"Management expects earnings growth to slow down at least in the first half of 1997, a significant increase in high-grade steel market conditions is only expected toward the end of 1997," it said.

On the positive side, Boehler noted it expected higher export margins and an increase in market share for the current year. Incoming orders in the first two months of the year were already five percent above last year's level, it said.

"After the defensive years of restructuring, the group will now embark on the road of growth," the company said, adding that continued cost cutting efforts should have a positive impacts on this year's earnings.

Group sales in 1996 fell to 17.086 billion schillings from 18.272 billion schillings as Boehler concentrated on its core activities and some 400 schillings in sales of its welding technology unit were excluded because of a change in the accounting year of that unit.
Boehler noted it managed to keep prices on a steady level and that the stronger U.S. dollar, Italian lira and Swedish krona had helped to keep the decline in sales in check.
The group's shares were indicated almost two percent higher at 829 schillings in pre-bourse trade on the Vienna stock exchange.
